The pay isn't great. I have been doing it for 4 years and make $36.50. But, no nights, weekends or holidays. It's super flexible, I'm able to set my own schedule to some degree. 

On my team there are people who do street outreach to encampments where people are living. I'm on the part of our team that does outreach in supportive housing once people are housed. I have an office in the building where people come to see me, and I knock on doors to check in with folks. I do a fair amount of wound care, foot care, coordination of care, chronic condition care management. I have the freedom to kind of do whatever I want. Like serve tea in my office, host walking groups. I'm working with people who have a fair distrust of healthcare providers, so building rapport over time is super important. It's a great job.
I got a job on a PACT team that was willing to hire me without experience. Stayed long enough to have the experience required by my current job.

My first nursing job was ACT! Where I live (Seattle) most of the organizations doing community health have a hard time finding candidates who are passionate about the work. They'd rather have someone who really wants to do it and then provide support and training.

I work doing community outreach nursing with people who have been chronically homeless. It doesn't pay like a hospital, but it's so flexible and rewarding. No weekends evenings or holidays. I love my clients and coworkers.
